title: Conflicts between mods
description:
Find mods that change the same thing, and say which one wins.

```
better-swords sets item.sword.damage = 8
balance-patch sets item.sword.damage = 6
conflict: item.sword.damage (better-swords 8, balance-patch 6) -> balance-patch wins (loaded later)
no conflict: item.bow.range (only one mod)
```
hints: Keep `std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>>>` of key to every (mod, value) that set it (lesson 13.07).
The last one in load order is the winner; that is why load order matters.
requirements: Each mod is a list of `key = value` changes.
Apply mods in load order; record every key set by more than one mod.
Print the conflicts and the final values.
stretch: Let a mod mark a change as "merge" for lists (add items instead of replacing).
